Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

module FixturesTestHelper
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def identify(label, column_type = :integer)
      if label.to_s.end_with?("_uuid")
        column_type = :uuid
        label = label.to_s.delete_suffix("_uuid")
      end

      # Rails passes :string for varchar columns, so handle both :uuid and :string
      return super(label, column_type) unless column_type.in?([ :uuid, :string ])
      generate_fixture_uuid(label)
    end

    private

    def generate_fixture_uuid(label)
      # Generate deterministic UUIDv7 for fixtures that sorts by fixture ID
      # This allows .first/.last to work as expected in tests
      # Use the same CRC32 algorithm as Rails' default fixture ID generation
      # so that UUIDs sort in the same order as integer IDs
      fixture_int = Zlib.crc32("fixtures/#{label}") % (2**30 - 1)

      # Translate the deterministic order into times in the past, so that records
      # created during test runs are also always newer than the fixtures.
      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision
      # Extract fractional milliseconds and convert to 12-bit value (0-4095)
      # This gives us ~0.244 microsecond precision
      frac_ms = time_ms - timestamp_ms
      sub_ms_precision = (frac_ms * 4096).to_i & 0xfff

      # Derive deterministic "random" bits from seed_string for the remaining random bits
      hash = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(seed_string)

      # 12-bit sub-ms precision + 4-bit version (0111 for v7)
      bytes[6] = ((sub_ms_precision >> 8) & 0x0f) | 0x70  # version 7
      bytes[7] = sub_ms_precision & 0xff

      # 2-bit variant (10) + 62-bit random
      rand_b = hash[3...19].to_i(16) & ((2**62) - 1)
      bytes[8] = ((rand_b >> 56) & 0x3f) | 0x80  # variant 10
      bytes[9] = (rand_b >> 48) & 0xff
      bytes[10] = (rand_b >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[11] = (rand_b >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[12] = (rand_b >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[13] = (rand_b >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[14] = (rand_b >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[15] = rand_b & 0xff

      # Format as UUID string and convert to base36 (25 chars)
      uuid = "%02x%02x%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x" % bytes
      ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.hex_to_base36(uuid.delete("-"))
    end
  end
end

    end

class Account::DataTransfer::RecordSetTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @importable_model_names = %w[ Card Board Event ]
  end

  test "check rejects polymorphic type not in the importable models allowlist" do
    event_data = build_event_data(eventable_type: "Identity")

    record_set = Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet.new(account: importing_account, model: Event, importable_model_names: @importable_model_names)

    error = assert_raises(Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::IntegrityError) do

require "test_helper"

class Cards::CommentsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in_as :kevin
  end

  test "create" do
    assert_difference -> { cards(:logo).comments.count }, +1 do
      post card_comments_path(cards(:logo)), params: { comment: { body: "Agreed." } }, as: :turbo_stream
    end

    assert_response :success
  end

  test "create on draft card is forbidden" do
    draft_card = boards(:writebook).cards.create!(status: :drafted, creator: users(:kevin))

    assert_no_difference -> { draft_card.comments.count } do
      post card_comments_path(draft_card), params: { comment: { body: "This should be forbidden" } }, as: :json
    end

    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "update" do
    put card_comment_path(cards(:logo), comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)), params: { comment: { body: "I've changed my mind" } }, as: :turbo_stream

    assert_response :success
    assert_action_text "I've changed my mind", comments(:logo_agreement_kevin).reload.body
  end

  test "update another user's comment" do
    assert_no_changes -> { comments(:logo_agreement_jz).reload.body.to_s } do
      put card_comment_path(cards(:logo), comments(:logo_agreement_jz)), params: { comment: { body: "I've changed my mind" } }, as: :turbo_stream
    end

    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "index as JSON" do
    card = cards(:logo)

    get card_comments_path(card), as: :json

    assert_response :success
    assert_equal card.comments.count, @response.parsed_body.count
  end

  test "create as JSON" do
    card = cards(:logo)

    assert_difference -> { card.comments.count }, +1 do
      post card_comments_path(card), params: { comment: { body: "New comment" } }, as: :json
    end

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal card_comment_path(card, Comment.last, format: :json), @response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal Comment.last.id, @response.parsed_body["id"]
  end

  test "create as JSON with custom created_at" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    custom_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 15, 10, 30, 0)

    assert_difference -> { card.comments.count }, +1 do
      post card_comments_path(card), params: { comment: { body: "Backdated comment", created_at: custom_time } }, as: :json
    end

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal custom_time, Comment.last.created_at
  end

  test "show as JSON" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)

    get card_comment_path(comment.card, comment), as: :json

    assert_response :success
    assert_equal comment.id, @response.parsed_body["id"]
    assert_equal comment.card.id, @response.parsed_body.dig("card", "id")
    assert_equal card_url(comment.card), @response.parsed_body.dig("card", "url")
    assert_equal card_comment_url(comment.card, comment), @response.parsed_body["url"]
  end

  test "create as JSON with flat params" do
    card = cards(:logo)

    assert_difference -> { card.comments.count }, +1 do
      post card_comments_path(card), params: { body: "Flat comment" }, as: :json
    end

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "Flat comment", Comment.last.body.to_plain_text
  end

  test "update as JSON with flat params" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)

    put card_comment_path(cards(:logo), comment), params: { body: "Flat update" }, as: :json

    assert_response :success
    assert_equal "Flat update", comment.reload.body.to_plain_text

    assert_equal comment.id, json["id"]
    assert_equal "Flat update", json["body"]["plain_text"]
  end

    put card_comment_path(cards(:logo), comment), params: { comment: { body: "Updated comment" } }, as: :json

    assert_equal comment.id, json["id"]

require "test_helper"

class CommentTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Current.session = sessions(:david)
  end

  test "cannot create comment on a draft card" do
    draft_card = cards(:unfinished_thoughts)

    comment = draft_card.comments.build(body: "This should fail")

    assert_not comment.valid?
    assert_includes comment.errors[:card], "does not allow comments"

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
      draft_card.comments.create!(body: "This should raise")
    end
  end

  test "rich text embed variants are processed immediately on attachment" do
    comment = cards(:logo).comments.create!(body: "Check this out")
    comment.body.body.attachables # force load

    blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload! \
      io: File.open(file_fixture("moon.jpg")),
      filename: "moon.jpg",
      content_type: "image/jpeg"

    comment.body.body = ActionText::Content.new(comment.body.body.to_html).append_attachables(blob)
    comment.save!

    embed = comment.body.embeds.sole

    Attachments::VARIANTS.each_key do |variant_name|
      variant = embed.variant(variant_name)
      assert variant.processed?, "Expected #{variant_name} variant to be processed immediately"
    end
  end
end

  def load_schema!

    super

  private
    def define_uuid_primary_key_pending_default

# Apply MySQL-compatible column limits when defining tables.
#
# For string columns: defaults to 255 (MySQL's VARCHAR default)
#
# For text columns: converts MySQL's `size:` option to equivalent limits:
#   - (blank/default): 65,535 (TEXT)
#   - size: :tiny: 255 (TINYTEXT)
#   - size: :medium: 16,777,215 (MEDIUMTEXT)
#   - size: :long: 4,294,967,295 (LONGTEXT)
#

module TableDefinitionColumnLimits
  TEXT_SIZE_TO_LIMIT = {
    tiny: 255,
    medium: 16_777_215,
    long: 4_294_967_295
  }.freeze

  TEXT_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 65_535
  STRING_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 255

  def column(name, type, **options)
    if type == :string
      options[:limit] ||= STRING_DEFAULT_LIMIT
    end

    if type == :text || type == :binary
      if options.key?(:size)
        size = options.delete(:size)
        options[:limit] ||= TEXT_SIZE_TO_LIMIT.fetch(size) do
          raise ArgumentError, "Unknown text size: #{size.inspect}. Use :tiny, :medium, or :long"
        end
      elsif type == :text
        options[:limit] ||= TEXT_DEFAULT_LIMIT
      end
    end

    super
  end
end

# For SQLite: append inline CHECK constraints to enforce string/text length limits.
# since SQLite doesn't natively enforce VARCHAR/TEXT length limits.
module SQLiteColumnLimitCheckConstraints
  def add_column_options!(sql, options)
    super

    column = options[:column]
    if column && column.limit && %i[string text].include?(column.type)
      check_expr = if column.type == :string
        # VARCHAR limits are in characters
        %(length("#{column.name}") <= #{column.limit})
      else
        # TEXT limits are in bytes
        %(length(CAST("#{column.name}" AS BLOB)) <= #{column.limit})
      end
      sql << " CHECK(#{check_expr})"
    end

    sql
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
  ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::TableDefinition.prepend(TableDefinitionColumnLimits)
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record_sqlite3adapter) do
  ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::SQLite3::SchemaCreation.prepend(SQLiteColumnLimitCheckConstraints)
end

class Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  class IntegrityError < StandardError; end
  class ConflictError < IntegrityError; end

  IMPORT_BATCH_SIZE = 100
  INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES = %w[Export Account::Import].freeze

  attr_accessor :importable_model_names
  attr_reader :account, :model, :attributes

  def initialize(account:, model:, attributes: nil, importable_model_names: nil)
    @account = account
    @model = model
    @attributes = (attributes || model.column_names).map(&:to_s)
    @importable_model_names = importable_model_names || [ model.name ]
  end

  def export(to:, start: nil)
    with_zip(to) do
      block = lambda do |record|
        export_record(record)
      end

      records.respond_to?(:find_each) ? records.find_each(&block) : records.each(&block)
    end
  end

  def import(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      file_list = files
      file_list = skip_to(file_list, start) if start

      file_list.each_slice(IMPORT_BATCH_SIZE) do |file_batch|
        import_batch(file_batch)
        callback&.call(record_set: self, files: file_batch)
      end
    end
  end

  def check(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      file_list = files
      file_list = skip_to(file_list, start) if start

      file_list.each do |file_path|
        check_record(file_path)
        callback&.call(record_set: self, file: file_path)
      end
    end
  end

  private
    attr_reader :zip

    def with_zip(zip)
      old_zip = @zip
      @zip = zip
      yield
    ensure
      @zip = old_zip
    end

    def records
      model.where(account_id: account.id)
    end

    def export_record(record)
      zip.add_file "data/#{model_dir}/#{record.id}.json", record.attributes.slice(*attributes).to_json
    end

    def files
      zip.glob("data/#{model_dir}/*.json")
    end

    def import_batch(files)
      batch_data = files.map do |file|
        data = load(file)
        data.slice(*attributes).merge("account_id" => account.id).tap do |record_data|
          record_data["updated_at"] = Time.current if record_data.key?("updated_at")
        end
      end

      model.insert_all!(batch_data)
    end

    def check_record(file_path)
      data = load(file_path)
      expected_id = File.basename(file_path, ".json")

      unless data["id"].to_s == expected_id
        raise IntegrityError, "#{model} record ID mismatch: expected #{expected_id}, got #{data['id']}"
      end

      missing = attributes - data.keys
      if missing.any?
        raise IntegrityError, "#{file_path} is missing required fields: #{missing.join(', ')}"
      end

      if model.exists?(id: data["id"])
        raise ConflictError, "#{model} record with ID #{data['id']} already exists"
      end

      check_associations_dont_exist(data)
    end

    def check_associations_dont_exist(data)
      model.reflect_on_all_associations(:belongs_to).each do |association|

      else
        associated_class = association.klass

      end
    end

**Analyzing Reaction Updates: A Deep Dive into Turbo Stream Strategies**

Okay, let's break this down. We're talking about how to best handle real-time updates to reactions on a card, particularly when multiple users are involved. We've got two main approaches in mind: Option A, which is the `broadcasts_refreshes_to` method, and Option B, which is direct Turbo Stream broadcasts using `broadcast_append_to` and `broadcast_remove_to`. We need to analyze each of them meticulously.

With Option A, the `Reaction` model would have `broadcasts_refreshes_to :card`, or a related call to refresh the card (or a similar construct), triggering a full refresh of the card when a reaction is created or destroyed. This leverages the `touch` method and `after_commit` hooks. The key here is the `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob` sending a refresh signal. The interesting part is how Turbo handles the request ID, preventing the originating user from receiving their own refresh (which is awesome!). This allows for immediate updates for the user who added the reaction through the HTTP response, while other users on the same page will receive a seamless update, because Turbo fetches the latest version of the card in the background. We have to consider scenarios like the user typing in an input form, and if the refresh will obliterate that. If we are careful with `turbo-frame` and `data-controller="morph-guard"` we can protect those inputs. This also has to be combined with careful use of `data-turbo-permanent` and caching. I'm also carefully checking how the touches chain up to the `card`, since we want the card to be refreshed, but not through an unnecessary number of broadcasts.

Now, Option B. This is where we directly broadcast Turbo Streams from the `Reaction` model, using `broadcast_append_to` and `broadcast_remove_to`. This would involve appending the reaction directly to the DOM via ActionCable. The big red flag I see immediately is the potential for *duplicate* reactions, because the initiating user gets the initial response from the `create.turbo_stream.erb` template, but then also receives the ActionCable broadcast (since `append` broadcasts don't have the same request ID suppression as `refresh`). This is bad. We could try relying *solely* on ActionCable for the append, but that causes issues in tests, and doesn't offer instant feedback to the user, and if they have a slow connection... this is all just a bad idea.

So, Option A, with `broadcasts_refreshes_to :card`, seems far superior, avoiding the duplicate reaction issue and offering a cleaner, more robust approach. We can take advantage of Turbo's refresh logic and request ID suppression to deliver a seamless user experience, preserving in-progress edits and drafts by protecting them with `morph-guard` and `data-turbo-permanent`. This approach offers a clear separation of concerns and a better approach to real-time updates.

Brilliant! Everyone else – including other tabs of the same user – receives the `<turbo-stream action="refresh">`, gets the background fetch, and the DOM morphs cleanly. Excellent implementation!

Wait, hold on a second. There’s one more subtle thing to consider with `broadcasts_refreshes_to`. Let's really dig into this now...

Let's think through **Option A**: what's the behavior when a user (let's call them User A) creates or destroys a reaction?

Wait... if a `reaction` is destroyed, the `after_commit` block *should* run: `broadcasts_refreshes_to` will execute `after_commit -> { broadcast_refresh_later_to(stream.try(:call, self) || send(stream)) }`! # after the debounced logic triggers.
class Turbo::ThreadDebouncer
  delegate :wait, to: :debouncer

  class_attribute :debouncer_class, default: Turbo::Debouncer

  def self.for(key, delay: Turbo::Debouncer::DEFAULT_DELAY)
    Thread.current[key] ||= new(key, Thread.current, delay: delay)
  end

  private_class_method :new

  def initialize(key, thread, delay: )
    @key = key
    @debouncer = debouncer_class.new(delay: delay)
    @thread = thread
  end

  def debounce
    debouncer.debounce do
      yield.tap do
        thread[key] = nil
      end
    end
  end

  private
    attr_reader :key, :debouncer, :thread
end

  attr_reader :delay, :scheduled_task

  DEFAULT_DELAY = 0.5

  def initialize(delay: DEFAULT_DELAY)
    @delay = delay
    @scheduled_task = nil
  end

  def debounce(&block)
    scheduled_task&.cancel unless scheduled_task&.complete?
    @scheduled_task = Concurrent::ScheduledTask.execute(delay, &block)
  end

  def wait
    scheduled_task&.wait(wait_timeout)
  end

  private

      delay + 1

      #
      # In addition to a String, the helper also accepts an Object or Array to

      #       message.broadcast_remove
      #     end
      #
      #     assert_equal "replace", replace["action"]
      #     assert_equal "replace", remove["action"]
      #
      def capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts(stream_name_or_object, &block)
        stream_name = stream_name_from(stream_name_or_object)
        payloads = if block_given?
          new_broadcasts_from(broadcasts(stream_name), stream_name, "capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts", &block)
        else
          broadcasts(stream_name)
        end

        payloads.flat_map do |payload|
          html = ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(payload)
          document = Nokogiri::HTML5.parse(html)

          document.at("body").element_children
        end
      end

module VcrTestHelper
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    class_attribute :vcr_record

    setup do
      @casette_name = "#{self.class.name.tableize.singularize}-#{name}"
      VCR.insert_cassette @casette_name,
        record: recording? ? :all : :none,
        preserve_exact_body_bytes: true
    end

    teardown do
      VCR.eject_cassette
    end

    def recording?
      vcr_record || ENV["VCR_RECORD"]
    end
  end

  class_methods do
    # Use to force record mode at development time: always perform real http interactions and record fixtures
    def vcr_record!
      raise "#vcr_record! is meant for dev time. You are not supposed to run it in CI." if ENV["CI"]

      self.vcr_record = true
    end
  end

  def without_vcr_body_matching(&block)
    VCR.use_cassette("#{@casette_name}_without_body", match_requests_on: [ :method, :uri ], &block)
  end
end

  # Fixed EC P-256 key pair for WebAuthn tests.
  WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY = OpenSSL::PKey::EC.new(
    [ "307702010104201dd589de7210b3318620f32150e3012cce021519df1d6e9e01" \
      "0471146d395cdca00a06082a8648ce3d030107a14403420004116847fe19e1ad" \
      "4471ab9980d7ff9cc1e4c7cb7a3af00e082b64fcd84f5ae70114c2495eef16f" \
      "542b5e57dd1b263661624e3cf28f581b57a441edbd756a41d0e" ].pack("H*")
  )

  # Pre-encoded COSE EC2/ES256 public key (CBOR) for the key above.
  # {1: 2, 3: -7, -1: 1, -2: <x 32 bytes>, -3: <y 32 bytes>}
  COSE_PUBLIC_KEY = [ "a5010203262001215820116847fe19e1ad4471ab9980d7ff9cc1" \
    "e4c7cb7a3af00e082b64fcd84f5ae70122582014c2495eef16f542b5e57dd1b2" \
    "63661624e3cf28f581b57a441edbd756a41d0e" ].pack("H*")

  # CBOR prefix for {"fmt": "none", "attStmt": {}, "authData": bytes(164)}.
  # Auth data is always 164 bytes: rp_id_hash(32) + flags(1) + sign_count(4)
  # + aaguid(16) + credential_id_length(2) + credential_id(32) + cose_key(77).
  ATTESTATION_OBJECT_CBOR_PREFIX =
    [ "a363666d74646e6f6e656761747453746d74a068617574684461746158a4" ].pack("H*")

  private
    def request_webauthn_challenge(purpose: "authentication")
      untenanted { post my_passkey_challenge_url, params: { purpose: purpose } }
      response.parsed_body["challenge"]
    end

    def webauthn_challenge(purpose: nil)
      ActionPack::WebAuthn::PublicKeyCredential::Options.new(challenge_purpose: purpose).challenge
    end

    def webauthn_private_key
      WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY
    end

    def build_attestation_params(challenge:)
      credential_id = SecureRandom.random_bytes(32)
      auth_data = build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id: credential_id)

      {
        passkey: {
          client_data_json: webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.create"),
          attestation_object: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(ATTESTATION_OBJECT_CBOR_PREFIX + auth_data, padding: false),
          transports: [ "internal" ]
        }
      }
    end

    def build_assertion_params(challenge:, credential:, sign_count: 1)
      client_data_json = webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.get")
      authenticator_data = build_assertion_auth_data(sign_count: sign_count)
      signature = webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)

      {
        passkey: {
          id: credential.credential_id,
          client_data_json: client_data_json,
          authenticator_data: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(authenticator_data, padding: false),
          signature: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(signature, padding: false)
        }
      }
    end

    def webauthn_client_data_json(challenge:, type:)
      { challenge: challenge, origin: "http://www.example.com", type: type }.to_json
    end

    # Attestation auth data includes the attested credential (public key + credential ID).
    def build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id:)
      [
        Digest::SHA256.digest("www.example.com"),   # rp_id_hash
        [ 0x45 ].pack("C"),                         # flags: UP + UV + AT
        [ 0 ].pack("N"),                            # sign_count
        "\x00" * 16,                                # aaguid
        [ credential_id.bytesize ].pack("n"),       # credential_id_length
        credential_id,
        COSE_PUBLIC_KEY
      ].join.b
    end

    # Assertion auth data is simpler — no attested credential.
    def build_assertion_auth_data(sign_count:)
      [
        Digest::SHA256.digest("www.example.com"),
        [ 0x05 ].pack("C"),                         # flags: UP + UV
        [ sign_count ].pack("N")
      ].join.b
    end

    def webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)
      signed_data = authenticator_data + Digest::SHA256.digest(client_data_json)
      WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY.sign("SHA256", signed_data)
    end

I need to confirm that.

**Crucially, `comment.touch` triggered `Card`'s `broadcasts_refreshes`!** This explains the output.  `comment.touch` causes the `card` to be touched. This, in turn, enqueues a `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob` for `Card`, `Board`, and even `[Account, :all_boards]`. I'm seeing the `<turbo-stream action="refresh"></turbo-stream>` being enqueued.

HOLD ON! Let's follow the data with `belongs_to :reactable, polymorphic: true, touch: true`!

When a `Reaction` is created on a `comment`:
*   `reaction` touches `comment` - causing the `comment` to touch the `card`, triggering a broadcast of the `<turbo-stream action="refresh">` for `@card`!
*   `comment.updated_at` changes, automatically invalidating `cache comment do`.

Now, if a `Reaction` is destroyed:
*   `reaction` touches `comment` - causing the `comment` to touch the `card`, triggering a broadcast of the `<turbo-stream action="refresh">` for `@card`!
*   `comment.updated_at` changes, automatically invalidating `cache comment do`.

Now, I have to stop and consider two very important points:

**Testing `broadcasts_refreshes` Reliability**

#### Question 1: I need to verify that `Card`'s `broadcasts_refreshes` functions reliably in a two-browser, two-user system test without relying on `perform_enqueued_jobs` or other workarounds.

I'm checking `config/environments/test.rb` and `test/application_system_test_case.rb` for clues.  In the `test` environment, `ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter` is `:test`. That means jobs are *not* automatically executed unless `perform_enqueued_jobs` is called, which could give us a false sense of reliability.  In `development` and `production`, Solid Queue executes `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob` asynchronously.  I need to consider what happens if someone is testing with `broadcast_refresh_later` versus `broadcast_refresh`.

Interestingly, the `card_refresh_test.rb` uses `broadcasts_refreshes` (which internally uses `broadcast_refresh_later`). This already enqueues `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob`.  Why did `perform_enqueued_jobs` *immediately* find the job, bypassing any 0.5s delay?  I need to dig into `turbo-rails` to figure out why the `Turbo::Debouncer` isn't delaying in that test. module Mentions
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :mentions, as: :source, dependent: :destroy
    has_many :mentionees, through: :mentions
    after_save_commit :create_mentions_later, if: :should_create_mentions?
  end

  def create_mentions(mentioner: Current.user)
    scan_mentionees.each do |mentionee|
      mentionee.mentioned_by mentioner, at: self
    end
  end

  def mentionable_content
    rich_text_associations.collect { send(it.name)&.to_plain_text }.compact.join(" ")
  end

  def scan_mentionees
    mentionees_from_attachments & mentionable_users
  end

  private
    def mentionees_from_attachments
      rich_text_associations.flat_map { send(it.name)&.body&.attachments&.collect { it.attachable } }.compact
    end

    def mentionable_users
      board.users
    end

    def rich_text_associations
      self.class.reflect_on_all_associations(:has_one).filter { it.klass == ActionText::RichText }
    end

    def should_create_mentions?
      mentionable? && (mentionable_content_changed? || should_check_mentions?)
    end

    def mentionable_content_changed?
      rich_text_associations.any? { send(it.name)&.body_previously_changed? }
    end

    def create_mentions_later
      Mention::CreateJob.perform_later(self, mentioner: Current.user)
    end

    # Template method
    def mentionable?
      true
    end

    def should_check_mentions?
      false

# Storage tracking is a business abstraction - we count what users upload.
# Original upload bytes only; variants/previews/derivatives excluded.
# Physical storage optimizations (deduplication, compression) don't affect quotas.
module Storage::Tracked
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_update :track_board_transfer, if: :board_transfer?
  end

  # Return self as the trackable record for storage entries
  def storage_tracked_record
    self
  end

  # Override in models where board is determined differently (e.g., Board itself)
  def board_for_storage_tracking
    board
  end

  # Total bytes for all attachments on this record
  def storage_bytes
    attachments_for_storage.sum { |a| a.blob.byte_size }
  end

  private
    def board_transfer?
      respond_to?(:will_save_change_to_board_id?) && will_save_change_to_board_id?
    end

    def track_board_transfer
      old_board = Board.find_by(id: attribute_in_database(:board_id))
      records = storage_transfer_records.compact
      return if records.empty?

      attachments_by_record = storage_attachments_for_records(records)

      attachments_by_record.each do |recordable, attachments|
        bytes = attachments.sum { |attachment| attachment.blob.byte_size }
        next if bytes.zero?

        # Debit old board
        if old_board
          Storage::Entry.record \
            account: account,
            board: old_board,
            recordable: recordable,
            delta: -bytes,
            operation: "transfer_out"
        end

        # Credit new board
        Storage::Entry.record \
          account: account,
          board: board,
          recordable: recordable,
          delta: bytes,
          operation: "transfer_in"
      end
    end

    def storage_transfer_records
      [ self ]
    end

    # Override if needed. Default = all direct attachments
    def attachments_for_storage(recordable = self)
      storage_attachments_for_records([ recordable ]).fetch(recordable, [])
    end

    def storage_attachments_for_records(recordables)
      records = Array(recordables).compact
      return {} if records.empty?

      # Build lookup for records by (type, id) to avoid N+1 when resolving RichText parents
      records_by_key = records.index_by { |r| [ r.class.name, r.id ] }

      rich_texts = ActionText::RichText.where(record: records)
      rich_text_to_parent = rich_texts.to_h { |rt| [ rt.id, records_by_key[[ rt.record_type, rt.record_id ]] ] }

      attachments = ActiveStorage::Attachment
        .where(record: records + rich_texts)
        .includes(:blob)
        .to_a

      attachments.each_with_object(Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = [] }) do |attachment, grouped|
        # Resolve parent without N+1: use lookup for RichText, direct for others
        recordable = if attachment.record_type == "ActionText::RichText"
          rich_text_to_parent[attachment.record_id]
        else
          records_by_key[[ attachment.record_type, attachment.record_id ]]
        end

        grouped[recordable] << attachment if recordable
      end
    end
end
"

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :pins, dependent: :destroy

    after_update_commit :broadcast_pin_updates, if: :preview_changed?
  end

  def pinned_by?(user)
    pins.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def pin_for(user)
    pins.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def pin_by(user)
    pins.find_or_create_by!(user: user)
  end

  def unpin_by(user)
    pins.find_by(user: user).tap { it.destroy }
  end

  private
    def broadcast_pin_updates
      pins.find_each do |pin|
        pin.broadcast_replace_later_to [ pin.user, :pins_tray ], partial: "my/pins/pin"
      end
    end
end

We need to make sure we aren't broadcasting refreshes for things that don't exist anymore. I realized the `card.destroyed?` check is key. Rails runs dependent destroys *before* setting `@destroyed = true`, and the `after_destroy_commit` runs *after* the transaction, so we need to be careful about timing and whether the card is freshly loaded to a nil reactable.

Then I realized this `destroyed_by_association` and `card.nil? || card.destroyed?` pattern is critical to handle cascade deletes. We need to skip the broadcast if the reaction is being destroyed because a comment or card is being destroyed.

But the real meat of this discussion is about choosing *how* to handle the broadcast, particularly in relation to the UI. There are multiple ways to do it, and they each have implications:

*   **Relying *only* on `touch: true` and `broadcasts_refreshes`**: Doesn't work immediately in tests with two browser sessions! Only broadcasts after 500ms when the job queue runs.
*   **Synchronous `broadcast_refresh_to`**: This solves the 2-session test immediately.
*   **Synchronous `broadcast_replace_to` and `broadcast_remove_to`**:  This method is the cleanest. Avoids many issues, especially with the double refresh of the sync method.

The problem with `broadcasts_refreshes` (the async one) is that it's too slow in tests without enqueuing jobs. So, using the synchronous, immediate broadcast is essential for the system tests. But then, it creates another problem.

The problem with the synchronous broadcast (as discovered in the comparison table) is that *if* we're also touching the `card`, there could be *two* refreshes: one immediate and one from the background job. This is not ideal because of visual issues, scroll-jank, and test confusion when calling `perform_enqueued_jobs`.

However, after comparing this, it's clear the immediate broadcast is crucial.

So what's the solution?

1.  Use `broadcast_refresh_to(card)` (synchronous).
2.  Use `broadcast_replace_to [card, :activity]` and `broadcast_remove_to`.

The synchronous method `broadcast_replace_to` is the ideal solution because it handles the problems of both methods.

Let's also look at how these are implemented:

*   `<turbo-stream action="refresh">` is super lightweight and *should* be quick and harmless as the channel can be empty (zero errors).
*   `turbo_stream_from` (using ActionCable) also ensures that broadcasts go to the correct channel.
*   A test is also required to verify synchronous broadcast with the appropriate `request_id` in order to ensure the test is robust.

I've also examined every CSS class, which has given me an even better understanding.

So, in summary:

*   **Synchronous `broadcast_replace_to` is the best approach.**
*   No need to modify `Card::Broadcastable` or the `card.updated_at` timestamps!
*   The system tests *must* pass immediately.

Clicking it again collapses the reaction. If they click *outside* the reaction area, the collapse action needs to trigger, making sure to handle overlapping reaction selections correctly. Crucially, when the user clicks the delete button, I have to ensure the form submits a `DELETE` request properly. I'll use the `turbo_stream.remove` response to remove the reaction from the DOM. Also, I'll add a `.reaction--deleting` class for a nice visual cue during the delete process.

For `reactions.yml`, I'm picturing this:

And remember, the other comments (`comments(:logo_agreement_jz)` and `comments(:layout_overflowing_david)`) have *zero* reactions initially. That's *gold* for testing the 0 -> 1 -> 0 transition. require "test_helper"

class ReactionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Current.session = sessions(:david)
  end

  test "validates presence and 16-character maximum of content" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)

    assert_not comment.reactions.build(content: "").valid?
    assert_not comment.reactions.build(content: "   ").valid?
    assert_not comment.reactions.build(content: nil).valid?

    assert comment.reactions.build(content: "a" * 16).valid?
    assert_not comment.reactions.build(content: "a" * 17).valid?

    assert comment.reactions.build(content: "🎉" * 16).valid?
    assert_not comment.reactions.build(content: "🎉" * 17).valid?
  end

  test "strips leading and trailing whitespace from content" do
    reaction = comments(:logo_agreement_jz).reactions.create!(content: "  Nice!  ")
    assert_equal "Nice!", reaction.content
  end

  test "defaults reacter to Current.user and account to reactable account" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)
    reaction = comment.reactions.create!(content: "🔥")

    assert_equal users(:david), reaction.reacter
    assert_equal comment.account, reaction.account
  end

  test "all_emoji? delegates to content" do
    assert reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_thumbs_up).all_emoji?
    assert_not reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_great).all_emoji?
    assert_not Reaction.new.all_emoji?
  end

  test "creating and destroying a reaction touches its comment" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)
    original_updated_at = comment.updated_at

    travel 5.seconds do
      reaction = comment.reactions.create!(content: "🎉")
      assert_operator comment.reload.updated_at, :>, original_updated_at

      created_updated_at = comment.updated_at
      travel 5.seconds do
        reaction.destroy!
        assert_operator comment.reload.updated_at, :>, created_updated_at
      end
    end
  end

  test "broadcasts refresh to card on create and destroy" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)
    card = comment.card
    reaction = nil

    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts card, count: 1 do
      reaction = comment.reactions.create!(content: "🔥")
    end

    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts card, count: 1 do
      reaction.destroy!
    end
  end

  test "destroying a comment destroys its reactions without broadcasting per reaction" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)
    assert_operator comment.reactions.count, :>, 0

    assert_no_turbo_stream_broadcasts comment.card do
      assert_difference -> { Reaction.count }, -comment.reactions.count do
        comment.destroy!
      end
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class Cards::Comments::ReactionsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in_as :kevin
  end

    get card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment)

    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".reactions"
    assert_select ".reactions__list .reaction", count: 2
    assert_select ".reactions__trigger img[src*='boost-color']"
  end

  test "index as JSON" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)

    get card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment), as: :json

    assert_response :success
    assert_equal 2, @response.parsed_body.count
    first = @response.parsed_body.first
    assert_equal reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_thumbs_up).id, first["id"]
    assert_equal "👍", first["content"]
    assert_equal users(:david).id, first.dig("reacter", "id")
    assert_equal card_comment_reaction_url(comment.card, comment, reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_thumbs_up)), first["url"]
  end

  test "new renders reaction form inside reacting turbo frame" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)

    get new_card_comment_reaction_path(comment.card, comment)

    assert_response :success
    assert_select "turbo-frame##{dom_id(comment, :reacting)}" do
      assert_select ".reaction.reaction__form.expanded"
      assert_select "input.reaction__input[maxlength='16']"
      assert_select ".reaction__submit-btn"
      assert_select ".reaction__cancel-btn"
      assert_select ".reaction__menu .reaction__emoji-list"
    end
  end

  test "create as turbo stream" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)

    assert_difference -> { comment.reactions.count }, +1 do
      post card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment),
        params: { reaction: { content: "🔥" } },
        as: :turbo_stream
    end

    assert_response :success
    assert_turbo_stream action: :append, target: dom_id(comment, :reactions_list)
    assert_turbo_stream action: :replace, target: dom_id(comment, :reacting)
  end

  test "create as JSON" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)

    assert_difference -> { comment.reactions.count }, +1 do
      post card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment),
        params: { reaction: { content: "Great 👍" } },
        as: :json
    end

    assert_response :created
    reaction = comment.reactions.last
    assert_equal "Great 👍", reaction.content
    assert_equal users(:kevin), reaction.reacter
    assert_equal reaction.id, @response.parsed_body["id"]
    assert_equal "Great 👍", @response.parsed_body["content"]
    assert_equal users(:kevin).id, @response.parsed_body.dig("reacter", "id")
  end

  test "create as JSON with flat params" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)

    assert_difference -> { comment.reactions.count }, +1 do
      post card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment),
        params: { content: "🎉" },
        as: :json
    end

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "🎉", @response.parsed_body["content"]
  end

  test "create rejects content over 16 characters" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)

    assert_no_difference -> { comment.reactions.count } do
      post card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment),
        params: { reaction: { content: "a" * 17 } },
        as: :json
    end

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    assert_no_difference -> { comment.reactions.count } do
      post card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment),
        params: { reaction: { content: "a" * 17 } },
        as: :turbo_stream
    end

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
  end

  test "create rejects blank content" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)

    assert_no_difference -> { comment.reactions.count } do
      post card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment),
        params: { reaction: { content: "   " } },
        as: :turbo_stream
    end

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
  end

  test "destroy own reaction as turbo stream" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)
    reaction = reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_great)

    assert_difference -> { comment.reactions.count }, -1 do
      delete card_comment_reaction_path(comment.card, comment, reaction), as: :turbo_stream
    end

    assert_response :success
    assert_turbo_stream action: :remove, target: dom_id(reaction)
  end

  test "destroy own reaction as JSON" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)
    reaction = reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_great)

    assert_difference -> { comment.reactions.count }, -1 do
      delete card_comment_reaction_path(comment.card, comment, reaction), as: :json
    end

    assert_response :no_content
  end

  test "cannot destroy another user's reaction" do
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)
    davids_reaction = reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_thumbs_up)

    assert_no_difference -> { comment.reactions.count } do
      delete card_comment_reaction_path(comment.card, comment, davids_reaction), as: :turbo_stream
    end

    assert_response :forbidden

    assert_no_difference -> { comment.reactions.count } do
      delete card_comment_reaction_path(comment.card, comment, davids_reaction), as: :json
    end

    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "inaccessible card returns not found" do
    sign_in_as :mike
    comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)

    get card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment), as: :json
    assert_response :not_found

    post card_comment_reactions_path(comment.card, comment), params: { reaction: { content: "👍" } }, as: :json
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "cached comment does not leak user-specific reaction markup across users" do
    card = cards(:logo)

    with_actionview_partial_caching do
      sign_in_as :david
      get card_path(card)
      assert_response :success
      david_comment_html = css_select("##{dom_id(comments(:logo_agreement_kevin))}").to_html

      sign_in_as :kevin
      get card_path(card)
      assert_response :success
      kevin_comment_html = css_select("##{dom_id(comments(:logo_agreement_kevin))}").to_html

      assert_equal david_comment_html, kevin_comment_html
    end
  end
end

cat <<'EOF' > test/system/comment_reactions_test.rb
require "application_system_test_case"

class CommentReactionsTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    @card = cards(:logo)
    @comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)
    @empty_comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)
  end

  test "adding, canceling, and removing comment reactions" do
    sign_in_as users(:david)
    visit card_url(@card)

    within_comment @empty_comment do
      # Initially has no reactions, only the trigger button with boost-color.svg
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger img[src*='boost-color']"

      # Clicking the trigger turns it into an input with confirm and cancel
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      assert_selector ".reaction.reaction__form.expanded"
      assert_selector "input.reaction__input[maxlength='16']"
      assert_selector ".reaction__submit-btn"
      assert_selector ".reaction__cancel-btn"
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__trigger"

      # Canceling restores the trigger button without adding a reaction
      find(".reaction__cancel-btn").click
      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"

      # Open again and cancel with Escape
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      assert_selector "input.reaction__input"
      find("input.reaction__input").send_keys(:escape)
      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"

      # Add a short text reaction
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "Love this!"
      find(".reaction__submit-btn").click

      # Reaction appears in the strip showing who left it, input is gone, button is back
      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      within ".reactions__list" do
        assert_selector ".reaction.reaction--deleteable", text: "Love this!"
        assert_selector ".reaction .reaction__avatar img[title='David']"
      end

      # Add a second reaction (emoji) using the button that is back
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "🎉"
      find(".reaction__submit-btn").click

      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      within ".reactions__list" do
        assert_selector ".reaction", count: 2
        assert_selector ".reaction span.txt-small.txt-medium", text: "🎉"
      end

      # Add a third reaction via the emoji picker menu
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find(".reaction__menu-btn").click
      assert_selector "dialog.reaction__popup[open]"
      within ".reaction__emoji-list" do
        click_on "Fire"
      end

      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      within ".reactions__list" do
        assert_selector ".reaction", count: 3
        assert_selector ".reaction span.txt-small.txt-medium", text: "🔥"
      end

      # Clicking own reaction reveals remove button; clicking outside collapses it
      love_reaction = find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Love this!")
      assert_no_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]} .reaction__delete"

      love_reaction.click
      assert_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]}.expanded .reaction__delete"

      # Clicking outside collapses it
      find(".comment__body").click
      assert_no_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]}.expanded"
      assert_no_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]} .reaction__delete"

      # Clicking own reaction again reveals remove button, clicking remove deletes it
      love_reaction.click
      within love_reaction do
        find(".reaction__delete").click
      end
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Love this!"
      assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", count: 2
    end
  end

  test "cannot reveal remove button on someone else's reaction" do
    sign_in_as users(:david)
    visit card_url(@card)

    within_comment @comment do
      davids_reaction = find("##{dom_id(reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_thumbs_up))}")
      kevins_reaction = find("##{dom_id(reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_great))}")

      assert davids_reaction[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable")
      assert_not kevins_reaction[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable")

      # Clicking Kevin's reaction does NOT reveal a remove button
      kevins_reaction.click
      assert_no_selector "##{kevins_reaction[:id]}.expanded"
      assert_no_selector "##{kevins_reaction[:id]} .reaction__delete"

      # Clicking David's own reaction DOES reveal a remove button
      davids_reaction.click
      assert_selector "##{davids_reaction[:id]}.expanded .reaction__delete"
    end
  end

  test "enforces 16 character maximum in the input" do
    sign_in_as users(:david)
    visit card_url(@card)

    within_comment @empty_comment do
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "12345678901234567890"
      assert_equal "1234567890123456", find("input.reaction__input").value

      find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
      assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "1234567890123456"
    end
  end

  test "everyone looking at the card sees reactions land and disappear in real time without reloading" do
    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      sign_in_as users(:david)
      visit card_url(@card)
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      sign_in_as users(:kevin)
      visit card_url(@card)
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"
      end
    end

    # David adds a reaction
    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        find(".reactions__trigger").click
        find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "Live! 🚀"
        find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀"
      end
    end

    # Kevin sees it land without reloading, and cannot delete David's reaction
    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀", wait: 5
        reaction_el = find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀")
        assert_not reaction_el[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable")
        reaction_el.click
        assert_no_selector "##{reaction_el[:id]} .reaction__delete"
      end
    end

    # Kevin starts typing a reaction while David adds another reaction — Kevin's input is preserved!
    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        find(".reactions__trigger").click
        find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "Draft"
      end
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        find(".reactions__trigger").click
        find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "🎉"
        find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉"
      end
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉", wait: 5
        assert_equal "Draft", find("input.reaction__input").value
        find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Draft"
      end
    end

    # David removes his "Live! 🚀" reaction; Kevin sees it vanish without reloading
    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Draft", wait: 5
        live_reaction = find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀")
        assert live_reaction[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable"), "Expected David's reaction to stay deleteable after morph"
        live_reaction.click
        within live_reaction do
          find(".reaction__delete").click
        end
        assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀"
      end
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀", wait: 5
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Draft"
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉"
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def within_comment(comment, &block)
      within("##{dom_id(comment)}", &block)
    end

    def wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
      assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all
    end
end

steps.reasoning_content:
**Debugging Triumph: A Classic Rails Callback Gotcha**

Okay, wow, just... wow. Look at that last line of output! `[[:broadcast_card_refresh, :after, [...]`! **WHAT A CLASSIC RAILS GOTCHA!!** I mean, I can't believe I missed this. We've got `after_create_commit :broadcast_card_refresh` and `after_destroy_commit :broadcast_card_refresh` in `app/models/reaction.rb`. And Rails, in its infinite... well, let's call it "wisdom"... combines those `:if` conditions (implicitly, using `AND`) when the **SAME CALLBACK METHOD NAME** is used with different commit hooks! So, `on: :create` AND `on: :destroy`, which is logically impossible to satisfy. **THAT'S WHY** `:broadcast_card_refresh` was **NEVER RUNNING**! It was always being short-circuited!

Thank goodness for those robust tests! Both our unit and multi-session system tests saved us here. *Phew!*

The fix? Either combine it into a single callback with `after_commit :broadcast_card_refresh, on: %i[ create destroy ]` (which is so clean and elegant!), or use two distinct method names. Using a single callback is by far the cleaner, more readable solution that avoids Rails' callback name deduplication and the unexpected behavior.

Now, let's tackle those other two test failures...

First, that `ReactionTest` failure. Ah, nested `travel` blocks. Rails doesn't like that. Just sequential calls to `travel ... do ... end` will fix that. Simple.

And finally, that `Cards::Comments::ReactionsControllerTest` failure. Why was `sign_in_as :mike` getting a `200 OK` on `cards(:logo)`? That smells like a permissions issue. I'll check `test/fixtures/accesses.yml` and `test/fixtures/boards.yml` to figure out which user does *not* have access to `boards(:writebook)` or `boards(:private)`. And let's find that bug!

steps.reasoning_content:
**A Deep Dive into a CSS Conundrum**

Okay, deep breath! Thank goodness we double-checked those computed rectangles in Chrome. The numbers are revealing a significant discrepancy. Look at these values: the form itself is roughly 350x34 pixels, but the menu button, submit button, and cancel button are all hovering around 42 pixels in height! This is a massive visual issue. How did these buttons, which should be within a 34px pill, end up at 42px instead of the expected 20px (1.25rem)?

My immediate focus is on `app/assets/stylesheets/reactions.css`, specifically lines 161-170. We can see the variables are being defined.  Here's where things get interesting: `--btn-size` seems to become 2rem (or 42px).

So, let's break this down. In headless Chrome, does `@media (any-hover: none)` match? Or is 1rem actually equal to 19px? Let's check the size of an "Emoji pill rect" (32.0625px) to help with the calculations. It seems the calculations point to an equivalent of 19px/rem (32.0625px / 1.6875rem = 19px/rem). Then, if 2rem is the assigned `--btn-size` and 1rem is 19px, then we get 2rem * 19px = 38px (scaled during the animation, 1.15x = 42px!).

Wait, why did `@media (any-hover: none)` match in headless Chrome? And, hold on, why did the "Form rect" have a height of 34.38? BECAUSE the `@keyframes react` animation at 50% is set to `transform: scale(1.15);` and we measured mid-animation (50ms after the click, approximately 1.07x).

Hold on, why was the Menu/Submit/Cancel button ~38px (~2rem) instead of ~23.75px (1.25rem)? Because headless Chrome has no pointing device, therefore `@media (any-hover: none)` is matching.  Let me try a `getComputedStyle(submit).getPropertyValue("--btn-size")` check. So, if headless Chrome matches `@media (any-hover: none)`, then `comments.css` sets `--reaction-size: 1.6875rem` (at `min-width: 640px`), while `reactions.css` sets `--btn-size: 2rem` at `@media (any-hover: none)`. *That's* the design's shipped CSS!

I need to verify this in Chrome *after* the 300ms animation has completed (so I'll sleep 0.4 seconds) AND check `matchMedia("(any-hover: none)").matches` and `getComputedStyle`. This should finally get to the bottom of this.

require "application_system_test_case"

class CommentReactionsTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    @card = cards(:logo)
    @comment = comments(:logo_agreement_kevin)
    @empty_comment = comments(:logo_agreement_jz)
  end

  test "adding, canceling, and removing comment reactions" do
    sign_in_as users(:david)
    visit card_url(@card)

    # System comments do not get a reactions strip
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(comments(:logo_5))} .reactions"

    within_comment @empty_comment do
      # Initially has no reactions, only the trigger button with boost-color.svg
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger img[src*='boost-color']"

      # Clicking the trigger turns it into an input with confirm and cancel
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      assert_selector ".reaction.reaction__form.expanded"
      assert_selector "input.reaction__input[maxlength='16']"
      assert_selector ".reaction__submit-btn"
      assert_selector ".reaction__cancel-btn"
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__trigger"

      # Blank / whitespace-only submission is prevented
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "   "
      find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
      assert_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"

      # Canceling restores the trigger button without adding a reaction
      find(".reaction__cancel-btn").click
      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"

      # Open again, open emoji menu, Escape closes only the emoji menu, second Escape cancels form
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find(".reaction__menu-btn").click
      assert_selector "dialog.reaction__popup[open]"
      find(".reaction__menu-btn").send_keys(:escape)
      assert_no_selector "dialog.reaction__popup[open]"
      assert_selector ".reaction__form"
      find("input.reaction__input").send_keys(:escape)
      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"

      # Add a short text reaction via confirm button
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "Love this!"
      find(".reaction__submit-btn").click

      # Reaction appears in the strip showing who left it, input is gone, button is back
      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      within ".reactions__list" do
        assert_selector ".reaction.reaction--deleteable", text: "Love this!"
        assert_selector ".reaction .reaction__avatar img[title='David']"
      end

      # Add a second reaction (emoji) using Enter key
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "🎉"
      find("input.reaction__input").send_keys(:enter)

      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      within ".reactions__list" do
        assert_selector ".reaction", count: 2
        assert_selector ".reaction span.txt-small.txt-medium", text: "🎉"
      end

      # Add a third reaction via the emoji picker menu
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find(".reaction__menu-btn").click
      assert_selector "dialog.reaction__popup[open]"
      within ".reaction__emoji-list" do
        click_on "Fire"
      end

      assert_no_selector ".reaction__form"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
      within ".reactions__list" do
        assert_selector ".reaction", count: 3
        assert_selector ".reaction span.txt-small.txt-medium", text: "🔥"
      end

      # Clicking own reaction reveals remove button; clicking outside collapses it
      love_reaction = find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Love this!")
      assert_no_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]} .reaction__delete"

      love_reaction.click
      assert_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]}.expanded .reaction__delete"

      find(".comment__body").click
      assert_no_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]}.expanded"
      assert_no_selector "##{love_reaction[:id]} .reaction__delete"

      # Clicking own reaction again reveals remove button; clicking remove deletes it
      love_reaction.click
      within love_reaction do
        find(".reaction__delete").click
      end
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Love this!"
      assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", count: 2

      # Remove the remaining two reactions — list collapses cleanly and trigger remains usable
      find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉").click
      find(".reactions__list .reaction.expanded .reaction__delete").click
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉"

      find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🔥").click
      find(".reactions__list .reaction.expanded .reaction__delete").click
      assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"
      assert_selector ".reactions__trigger"
    end
  end

  test "cannot reveal remove button on someone else's reaction" do
    sign_in_as users(:david)
    visit card_url(@card)

    within_comment @comment do
      davids_reaction = find("##{dom_id(reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_thumbs_up))}")
      kevins_reaction = find("##{dom_id(reactions(:logo_agreement_kevin_great))}")

      assert davids_reaction[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable")
      assert_not kevins_reaction[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable")

      # Clicking Kevin's reaction does NOT reveal a remove button
      kevins_reaction.click
      assert_no_selector "##{kevins_reaction[:id]}.expanded"
      assert_no_selector "##{kevins_reaction[:id]} .reaction__delete"

      # Clicking David's own reaction DOES reveal a remove button
      davids_reaction.click
      assert_selector "##{davids_reaction[:id]}.expanded .reaction__delete"
    end
  end

  test "enforces 16 character maximum in the input" do
    sign_in_as users(:david)
    visit card_url(@card)

    within_comment @empty_comment do
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "12345678901234567890"
      assert_equal "1234567890123456", find("input.reaction__input").value

      find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
      assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "1234567890123456"
    end
  end

  test "newly posted comment immediately supports reactions" do
    sign_in_as users(:david)
    visit card_url(@card)

    fill_in_lexxy with: "Fresh comment for reacting"
    click_on "Post"

    assert_selector ".comment", text: "Fresh comment for reacting"
    new_comment_el = find(".comment", text: "Fresh comment for reacting")

    within new_comment_el do
      find(".reactions__trigger").click
      find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "Nice!"
      find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
      assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction.reaction--deleteable", text: "Nice!"
    end
  end

  test "everyone looking at the card sees reactions land and disappear in real time without reloading" do
    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      sign_in_as users(:david)
      visit card_url(@card)
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      sign_in_as users(:kevin)
      visit card_url(@card)
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction"
      end
    end

    # David adds a reaction
    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        find(".reactions__trigger").click
        find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "Live! 🚀"
        find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀"
      end
    end

    # Kevin sees it land without reloading, and cannot delete David's reaction
    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀", wait: 5
        reaction_el = find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀")
        assert_not reaction_el[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable")
        reaction_el.click
        assert_no_selector "##{reaction_el[:id]} .reaction__delete"
      end
    end

    # Kevin starts typing a reaction while David adds another reaction — Kevin's input is preserved!
    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        find(".reactions__trigger").click
        find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "Draft"
      end
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        find(".reactions__trigger").click
        find("input.reaction__input").fill_in with: "🎉"
        find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉"
      end
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉", wait: 5
        assert_equal "Draft", find("input.reaction__input").value
        find(".reaction__submit-btn").click
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Draft"
      end
    end

    # David removes his "Live! 🚀" reaction; Kevin sees it vanish without reloading
    Capybara.using_session(:david) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Draft", wait: 5
        live_reaction = find(".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀")
        assert live_reaction[:class].include?("reaction--deleteable"), "Expected David's reaction to stay deleteable after morph"
        live_reaction.click
        within live_reaction do
          find(".reaction__delete").click
        end
        assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀"
      end
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:kevin) do
      within_comment @empty_comment do
        assert_no_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Live! 🚀", wait: 5
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "Draft"
        assert_selector ".reactions__list .reaction", text: "🎉"
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def within_comment(comment, &block)
      within("##{dom_id(comment)}", &block)
    end

    def wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
      assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all
    end
end
EOF
